task: Multi-WhatsApp-account / multi-business support (local implementation + tests, no deploy)
summary: Multi-WhatsApp-account / multi-business support implemented locally (NOT deployed, NOT committed). One app, one login, one SQLite DB, one repo. New: whatsapp_accounts table + admin_account_access (migration 015, foreign-keys-off rebuild of business_settings/automation_settings (id = account id), reply_templates (PK account+key), customers (UNIQUE account+wa_id); whatsapp_account_id DEFAULT 1 added to conversations, customer_requests, notification_outbox, reply_activity, business_documents, offers; account 1 created from the existing business + whatsapp_qr_session row, auth_dir 'baileys-auth'). src/accounts/accountContext.ts (AsyncLocalStorage, legacy default 1) + accountRepo.ts (CRUD, enable/disable, session state, admin access model). qrConnection.ts rewritten as a per-account QrConnection class + manager map: own socket/auth dir (accounts/<id>/baileys-auth for new accounts; account 1 keeps data/baileys-auth), QR, reconnect, 401 archive, 515, owner marker, sent-ids; outbox sender routes by account; resumeQrConnection starts every enabled account; suspendQrConnection on disable (keeps creds). Pipeline runs inside the message's account; customer lock per (account, waId). Repos (customers, conversations, requests, outbox, templates, offers, documents, settings, automation, booking list, knowledge files per account under knowledge/accounts/<id>, dashboard data) take an explicit accountId defaulting to the context. Dashboard: accountMiddleware (X-Whatsapp-Account header validated server-side: unknown 404, forbidden 403, default = legacy), /api/dashboard/accounts CRUD + enable/disable + per-account QR endpoints, existing routes scoped, cross-account ids 404. UI: sidebar 'WhatsApp Accounts' list with status dots + switcher (localStorage), header account chip, Manage Accounts page (dashboard/pages-accounts.js). Docs: README 11a-bis, docs/QR_CONNECTION.md 'Multiple WhatsApp accounts'. .gitignore: knowledge/accounts/. Limitation: menu number structure (menuRouter.ts) stays shared; template texts are per account. Meta Cloud API path unchanged (legacy account). Port 3005 untouched; no deploy; local data/app.db and data/baileys-auth untouched (migration dry-run used a scratch COPY).
reason: User requested first-class multiple WhatsApp accounts/businesses in the existing application with isolated data and independent Baileys sessions, legacy data migrated to account 1 without re-pairing, one login, account switcher in the dashboard, comprehensive tests, no production deploy until authorised.

Migration dry run on a scratch COPY of local data/app.db (6 customers, 68 templates, 114 messages, connected session): counts unchanged, customer rows byte-identical, settings identical, account 1 connected with phone/jid carried over, foreign_key_check clean. Browser verification on a scratch data dir (port 3010, local .env, dev/mock providers): first-run setup, sidebar shows accounts with status, created 'Noor Salon' (Arabic name), switch updates chip/eyebrow, Connect for account 2 produced its own QR while account 1 kept its own pairing socket (2 sockets, generation 1 each). Scratch server stopped; temporary launch.json entry reverted. Not tested: real phone pairing of two numbers, Oracle deployment.
